reason: Selected method comparisons and consistency analysis support native tool-calling tests and repeated-trial evaluation.

candidates.title: Compare native tool calling with text-formatted action protocols
candidates.rule: For user-facing tool agents whose model supports native function calling, compare that interface with text-formatted ReAct before adding textual reasoning machinery.
candidates.passage: natively supported function calling consistently outperforms text-formatted agent methods
candidates.finding: Native calling outperforms text-based methods in the reported retail comparison. Reasoning helps text-formatted ReAct versus Act-only, but adding a think function to native calling does not boost performance.
models: GPT-4o and other historical state-of-the-art models in the method comparison
candidates.conditions: Domain policy and tool definitions are supplied; runs allow at most thirty actions. Agent temperature is zero and simulated user temperature is one.
candidates.limitations: User simulation is imperfect. These results do not establish that reasoning is useless inside a native tool-calling model or on different tasks. Exact token budgets may differ across interfaces.
candidates.validation_test: Compare native calling, text ReAct and Act-only with identical tools and policies; report task success, invalid arguments, latency and token cost.

candidates.title: Measure all-trial reliability alongside average agent success
candidates.rule: For customer-service agents, repeat each evaluation task and report the fraction consistently solved across trials alongside average one-run success.
candidates.finding: GPT-4o function calling has over 60% average retail success but under 25% consistency over eight trials. Repeated-trial reporting is inferred as a deployment check; it is not an intervention shown to improve reliability.
workloads: tau-retail simulated user and tool interactions
candidates.conditions: pass^k requires all k runs to succeed; pass@k measures at least one success and answers a different question.
candidates.limitations: Historical model and stochastic simulated users; the metric is not a production reliability guarantee or independent measurement of user harm. Do not treat pass@k as consistency.
candidates.validation_test: Repeat representative tasks with varied user phrasing and seeds. Report per-task failures, average success, all-trial success, confidence intervals and policy violations.

review_scope: Selected abstract, introduction, methods or main-result sections; not a comprehensive paper or appendix review.
